memory_update.text: For the AI accelerators + HBM node, NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, and MRVL form the most direct US-listed candidate set for this pass: merchant GPUs, HBM memory, and custom XPU silicon.

HBM exposure is not only a memory-supplier issue; accelerator designers and custom silicon vendors are tightly exposed through platform qualification, HBM stack count, bandwidth, power, packaging yield, and hyperscaler deployment schedules.

Non-US primary HBM leaders SK hynix and Samsung Electronics are central to the chokepoint but were not included as candidates because this pass requested US-listed companies. They remain mandatory comparables for HBM share, pricing, and capacity evidence.

TSMC is a highly relevant ADR-listed advanced packaging and foundry chokepoint for AI accelerators and HBM integration, but was left outside the five-candidate limit to keep this pass focused on accelerator/HBM product leaders. It should be covered in a dedicated advanced packaging / foundry node pass.

summary: Focused Layer 1B expansion for the AI accelerators + HBM memory node identified five US-listed companies with the most direct public-market exposure: NVIDIA and AMD as merchant AI accelerator platforms, Micron as the direct US-listed HBM memory supplier, and Broadcom and Marvell as custom AI accelerator / XPU silicon platforms. The node appears structurally important because modern AI accelerators bind together compute dies, HBM stacks, advanced packaging, networking I/O, and hyperscaler qualification cycles. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
